rv.q: Michael Longhurst’s pitch-perfect revival is now being offered up to a much wider demographic.
This is the brilliance of the show: Kushner burrows down into just two households, at a moment of huge global political change, to explore the realities of how change really comes about.
Moment by moment, the show offers a stunning experience, but overall it comes across as stylistically and dramatically unbalanced.
Not only is Clarke phenomenal with her voice and performance as Caroline but the show's themes around economic inequality are as urgent today as ever.

cn.t: Critics praise this Tony Kushner musical, with Sharon D Clarke's powerful performance and commanding voice earning particular acclaim. The show's exploration of change—both domestic and societal—in 1963 Louisiana resonates strongly.
